preamble: Raising and rounding of the open vowel [a] to the close back rounded [u]. It is attested as the end point of a backing-and-raising development of first-syllable *a in Chuvash (via intermediate [ɔ]/[o], still seen in the Lower Chuvash dialect), and as a direct raising of /ɒː/ (historical ā) before /n/ in colloquial Persian.

examples.note: Lower Chuvash keeps the intermediate stage ot; the change went *a > *å > o > u.
Historical ā (modern [ɒː]) raises to [u] before /n/ in colloquial speech.
